claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with an ML interatomic potential will substantially improve reference–ab initio configurational overlap.
Using an ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM references.
The proposed ML potential will be trained by active learning on ab initio energies and forces from relevant high-temperature configurations.
The target domain includes both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
The proposed composition domain is quinary or higher-component alloys.
The proposed temperature domain is approximately 0.8Tm to 1.1Tm.
High-entropy alloys exhibit broad local configurational disorder that an effective reference potential must cover.
An ML potential can provide expanded local-environment coverage for high-entropy-alloy liquids and near-melting solids.
Expanded local-environment coverage will allow the ML reference to mimic ab initio energies and forces more faithfully than EAM.
More faithful reproduction of ab initio energies and forces will improve reference–target phase-space overlap and mitigate path-length-driven integration errors.
EAM-based TOR-TILD exhibits large path mismatches for high-temperature liquid configurations.
The ML reference will produce systematically smaller free-energy discrepancies relative to ab initio than EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The reduction in path-integration error may be tens of meV per atom or more.
The method will be most effective for alloys with five or more components and significant atomic-size mismatch.
Performance may degrade over extremely wide composition ranges or for extremely high-melting systems.
Robust ML-potential fidelity requires extensive high-temperature ab initio training data.
The approach is less established for complex element combinations beyond selected quinary or senary alloys.
A decisive benchmark can compare ML-to-ab initio and EAM-to-ab initio integration paths and converged solid and liquid free energies against direct ab initio integration.
